changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For store-led retail deals, where the head of store operations or the COO is in the room: replace this line with the buyer's own words, 'One system for the tills and the website,' and follow it immediately with a live, step-by-step walkthrough of an online order being returned at a store till. Only use the walkthrough after the solutions engineer confirms it can be shown live. Do not describe it.
changes.why: Bev dismissed our line with 'that's a diagram.' She then asked how a return works 'Step by step. At the till.' and kept repeating 'One system for the tills and the website,' and we described the return instead of showing it.

changes.change: For retailers with store rollouts: add a line and a proof point on single accountability, framed around the buyer's fear: 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.' Name who owns installs and store rollout end to end. If partners do the installs, state that we are the one accountable party. Back the line with a template rollout plan covering 'Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills.' Bring someone who has run a store rollout to the store workshop.
changes.why: Our answer on installs was a partner, and nobody on our side had run a store rollout. Adyen offered rollout veterans and one contract, which speaks directly to the stated fear of two vendors pointing at each other.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For store-led retail deals: offer a peer retailer they can talk to, and line up a reference call that can be arranged quickly, instead of pointing to customer stories. Suggested line: 'Talk to a retailer who has rolled us out across their stores.'
changes.why: The buyer asked 'can I talk to them?' and we couldn't set up a call in time, while Adyen named retailers Angela knew.

changes.change: For retail pitches aimed at the COO and store operations: open with the store problem, not checkout conversion. Lead with 'Buy online, return in store' at the till and a loyalty program that works everywhere because it is 'one customer, one basket.' In retail copy, say 'the tills' rather than 'point of sale', 'in-person payments' or 'unified commerce'.
changes.why: The evaluation was triggered by store returns and split customer records. The customer described it as 'one customer, one basket' and 'the tills,' and never used our category terms.
